world_rules: The relay is a legal obligation: an operator who knows it is down must report and restore it.
The approach chart is the authority ships trust; correcting it officially takes a survey the district must fund.
The station keeps a paper log; every fault filed is permanent and auditable.

The 'distress relay' is a homing signal: live, it broadcasts the approach bearing taken from the official chart, so vessels steer onto that line; cut, it simply stops guiding (it does not withhold rescue calls).

The tide table gives water heights and times; the chart gives the reef's position. Jonas's corrections to the tide table (heights) are separate from, and do not reveal, his private reef soundings (position).
locations: the signal station on the point
